definition: Conformity is a type of social influence involving a change in belief or behaviour in order to fit in with a group.
Conformity is the tendency to change what we do, think or say in response to the influence of real or imagined pressure from others
yielding to group pressures
Conforming to majority opinions and behaviour publicly whilst privately maintaining your own.
Conforming publicly but continuing privately to disagree.
Conforming to majority opinions and behaviour whilst in the group, but you may not maintain these opinions and behaviours when you leave the group.
A moderate form of conformity where we act the same as the group because we share their values and want to be accepted. The change of belief or behaviour is often temporary.
Conforming to majority opinions and behaviour both publicly and privately, even when no longer a member of the group.
A deep type of conformity where a person conforms publicly and privately because they have internalised and accepted the views of the group. It is the deepest form of conformity
When a person is not in doubt but is influenced by social norms. The pressure comes from the group, based on a need to be liked and accepted.
Informational Social Influence is when uncertainty leads to a person adopting the behaviour of others – they conform because they don’t know what to do and they want to be correct.
Minority influence, is a form of social influence which takes place when a minority group, or possibly an individual, influences a majority to accept the minority's beliefs or behaviour.
Collectivist cultures, such as those of China, Korea, and Japan, emphasize family and work group goals above individual needs or desires.
Individualistic cultures (USA, UK, Italy) are more likely to have an independent view of themselves and view themselves as separate from others and define themselves based on their personal traits.
